description: Dalaran Heist bosses B (phase 8 family 15): fourteen encounters of The Dalaran Heist (Alchemist Wendy, Tala Stonerage, Disidra Stormglory, Linzi Redgrin, Vas'no, Bookmaster Bae Chao, Sharky McFin, Ranger Ar'ha, Jepetto Joybuzz, Dalaran Fountain Golem, Rasil Fireborne, Xur'ios, Mama Diggs, The Rat King) and their two boss cards (Hoard of Toys, Underbelly Rat). Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves the names against facts/violet-hold-2026-09.json, checks every card and writes data/dungeon-run/encounters-v1.json. The Heist hero cards print 30 Health (10 at level 1), so the tier is the boss's level from its wiki page: the page's own statement where it has one ("level 6 in Chapter 5", "levels 6-7", the final boss of Chapter 3), else the deck size of its table (the Heist boss deck grows with the level: 10 cards at level 1, 15 at 2, 20 at 3, 25 at 4-5, 30 from 6, as the pages' "missing 5 random cards" notes state); levels 1-2: tier 1; 3-4: tier 2; 5-6: tier 3; 7-8: tier 4 (the encounter model's level table).
method: The wiki's raw wikitext (?action=raw) was read for each boss page and the Normal column of its one deck table transcribed in table order, rowspan-aware, with the table's own counts; a "Possible cards" table has no counts and lists each card once. The page's "(card)" disambiguation suffix is dropped from a name. Boss-only cards and Murloc Tinyfin (no collectible engine card of that name) carry their id. Generated by verify/tools/gen/p8f15/make_f15.py.

adaptations.note: The Heist hero card prints 30 Health (10 for a level-1 boss) whatever level the boss is met at, so the tier is the level from the wiki: a table of possible cards for decks of 10 and 15 cards, the sizes of levels 1 and 2. Level 1 gives tier 1 (levels 1-2: tier 1; 3-4: tier 2; 5-6: tier 3; 7-8: tier 4 (the encounter model's level table)); the fight's Health is the act curve's at the floor.

The wiki lists 13 possible cards with no counts for a deck of 10 or 15 cards (the boss draws its deck from them). A combat tier fights with 30: each possible card once, then a second copy of each non-Legendary card in table order, then the curated Kabal and Mage fillers named in the row.

The wiki marks Equivalent Exchange (1) as auto-cast, so it is cast by rule, not by a choice of the boss's AI (DungeonRunEncounters.AutoCast, family 09's rule): at the start of the boss's turn, when it can pay the Cost and both hands hold a card, the Cost is paid and the power resolves. The engine never offers it as an option (it is registered with the passive powers). One random card of each hand changes sides (the game RNG): both leave their hands first, so a full hand never burns one, and each keeps its enchantments and Cost. Each side then knows the card it received (its own hand) and the card it gave (a hand-transfer fact, as Gloves of Mugging's); nothing else of either hand is shown.

Stormswell: after the boss casts a spell with Overload from its hand, a copy is cast again on the same target (RecastRules.Recast, Pirate's Mark's rule: a target that is gone loses only the targeted part; a Choose One copy keeps the option picked). The copy is a spell cast by an effect, so its Overload is owed too (the engine's rule, as for Yogg-Saron's casts), and it never casts again; a Secret or a Quest is not cast twice.

Jepetto is a chapter's final boss in the Heist; this mode has no major slot for Heist chapter finals (the Heist's major is its finale, family 18), so he is a tier 4 combat encounter.

Assembly: after either player draws a minion (mulligan replacements are not draws of the game), that player summons a 1/1 copy of the drawn card (Dollmaster Dorian's rule, Toyification DALA_BOSS_25e). The copy is a public summon, so the run player's drawn minion is revealed as Dorian's copy would reveal it; the boss's fair view does not use the reveal (its view of that hand stays masked).
Hoard of Toys (DALA_BOSS_25t, "Summon 1/1 copies of five random minions"): five random scripted minions of any class the run's generation filter allows, each summoned with Toyification (1/1).

Two listed cards cannot be in a boss deck here: Wee Spellstopper is a collectible card the engine does not script, and Glacial Mysteries puts one copy of each Secret of its owner's deck into play, a deck read the table does not admit for a boss. Scroll Savvy: a spell drawn costs (0) until the end of that turn (Savvy DALA_BOSS_28e, the rule of the Tombs passive Fleeting Knowledge). Excavate (1), "Deal 2 damage to a friendly Elemental. Find out what's inside.": the client data has no result table; the wiki's boss page lists the possible excavations ("Nothing; A Small Rock; Drawing 1-2 cards; Random shaman cards; Copy of the damaged minion; Dungeon Run treasures") with no odds. Here one of the six, each equally likely (the game RNG): nothing; A Small Rock (GILA_500p2t) to her hand; one or two draws (equally likely); one random scripted Shaman card from the pool the run's generation filter allows for the boss to her hand; a copy of the damaged minion's card to her hand; one of the sixteen Dungeon Run treasures King Togwaggle's Magic Candle finds (boss-admitted on catalog runs) to her hand. The 2 damage comes first; a full hand burns what is added.

Underbelly Rat, "When your hero dies, the eldest Underbelly Rat replaces your hero": when the boss's hero dies with an Underbelly Rat on his board (alive, not dying), the eldest (summoned first) leaves the board without dying and a new The Rat King enters through the row's script form (EncounterRules.SwapForm: hero and power fresh, Armor and weapon kept) with the rat's Health (its remaining Health of its maximum), as many times as he has rats. The same holds for a run player who controls a rat: that hero stays and takes the rat's Health. In the Heist's Chapter 4 every minion's Attack and Health were swapped (the chapter twist), so the rat fought as a 1/10 there; here it is the printed 10/1 unless a rule swaps it.
